title: Discrete Random Variables
intro: A discrete random variable takes countably many values. Its probability mass function lists their probabilities; its cumulative distribution function accumulates them.

blocks.caption: The PMF of a discrete random variable.

blocks.text: Any non-negative function that sums to 1 over a countable set is the PMF of some random variable, so a model can be specified directly by writing one down. Probabilities of events about $X$ are sums: $P(X\in A) = \sum_{x\in A}p_X(x)$.

blocks.caption: The CDF. It exists for every random variable, discrete or not.

blocks.text: For a discrete variable the CDF is a staircase: flat between possible values and jumping by $p_X(x)$ at each. Every CDF is non-decreasing, right-continuous, tends to 0 at $-\infty$ and to 1 at $+\infty$, and $P(a < X\le b) = F(b) - F(a)$. The size of a jump is a point probability: $P(X = x) = F(x) - F(x^-)$.

The indicator of an event, $\mathbf{1}_A$, is 1 when $A$ happens and 0 otherwise. It is the simplest random variable and one of the most useful: its distribution is Bernoulli with $P(\mathbf{1}_A = 1) = P(A)$, its expectation is $P(A)$, and counting random variables are sums of indicators, which is how many expectations are computed without knowing the full distribution (Expectation (#/probability/random-variables/expectation)).

blocks.source:
import numpy as np
from fractions import Fraction
# The PMF and CDF of S = sum of two fair dice
pmf = {s: Fraction(6 - abs(s - 7), 36) for s in range(2, 13)}
cdf, run = {}, Fraction(0)
for s in range(2, 13):
    run += pmf[s]; cdf[s] = run
print("s     :", " ".join(f"{s:>5}" for s in pmf))
print("P(S=s):", " ".join(f"{str(p):>5}" for p in pmf.values()))
print("F(s)  :", " ".join(f"{float(c):5.3f}" for c in cdf.values()))
print("sum of PMF =", sum(pmf.values()), "  P(4 <= S <= 9) = F(9) - F(3) =", cdf[9] - cdf[3])
# An indicator variable: its expectation is the probability of its event
rng = np.random.default_rng(5)
S = rng.integers(1, 7, (200000, 2)).sum(1)
print("mean of the indicator 1{S >= 10} =", round((S >= 10).mean(), 4), " exact =", float(sum(pmf[s] for s in (10, 11, 12))))

blocks.text: Output of the run: the PMF of the sum of two dice rises from 1/36 at 2 to 1/6 at 7 and falls back symmetrically; the CDF climbs from 0.028 to 1. The PMF sums to exactly 1 and $P(4\le S\le9) = F(9) - F(3) = 3/4$. The average of the indicator of $S\ge10$ over 200 000 simulated rolls is 0.167, matching $6/36$.

blocks.title: Reading a CDF
blocks.text: A CDF has $F(2) = 0.3$, $F(3^-) = 0.3$ and $F(3) = 0.55$. What is $P(X = 3)$, and what is $P(2 < X < 3)$?

blocks.title: The maximum of two dice
blocks.text: Find the PMF of $M = \max(D_1, D_2)$ for two fair dice.
solution: $P(M\le m) = (m/6)^2$, since both dice must be at most $m$.
